newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile Escondida workers said voting for strike.
newsitem.headline: Chile Escondida workers said voting for strike.

text.p: Workers at Chile's giant Escondida copper mine voting on whether to accept the latest company wage offer are mainly telling officials they want to continue striking, a union leader said Wednesday.
"Most of them are telling us that they are in favor of continuing the strike," Pablo Godoy, of the Chilean Mining Confederation, told Reuters by telephone.
Godoy, speaking from the bakers' union office which have been borrowed by the Escondida union for the vote, said he had spoken with workers after they cast their votes.

The 358 unionized workers at Escondida began voting at 1219 local (1619 GMT). Under Chilean law the voting urns cannot be opened for official counting of the results to begin until eight hours after the start of voting.
The rest of the mine's 2,000-strong workforce did not join the strike.
Mine CEO Ken Pickering said Wednesday that production was normal and shipments unaffected by the strike.
The 800,000-tonne-a-year mine is owned by Broken Hill Proprietary and RTZ-CRA.
